articles.title: Fuel prices going down for third straight week on November 24
articles.summary: Motorists get another round of relief as recovering supplies of global oil and weaker demand lead fuel prices to fall

blocks.text: REFUELING. Motorists queue at a gas station in Paco, Manila, to take advantage of a rollback in gasoline prices, October 20, 2026.
Rappler
Motorists get another round of relief as recovering supplies of global oil and weaker demand lead fuel prices to fall

MANILA, Philippines – Fuel prices are going down for a third consecutive week starting Tuesday, November 24, as international oil prices continue to decline amid expectations of improving global supplies.
The Department of Energy (DOE) announced the following minimum price decreases for November 24 to 30:

items: Gasoline – rollback of at least P3 per liter
Diesel – rollback of at least P2.60 per liter
Kerosene – rollback of at least P1.60 per liter

blocks.text: The adjustments follow last week’s reductions of P1.50 per liter for gasoline, P3.80 for diesel, and P5.80 for kerosene. Prior to that, gasoline prices plunged by P16.80 per liter, alongside rollbacks of P4.10 for diesel and P3.70 for kerosene.
This comes as global oil markets anticipate a supply surplus, with oil exports from the Middle East recovering and businesses and consumers cutting back on consumption.
However, the continuing US war on Iran and attacks on commercial vessels around the Strait of Hormuz remain risks to global supply.

Despite the recent rollbacks, local pump prices remain substantially higher than before the US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28. In the last full week before the conflict, common Metro Manila prices stood at around P54 to P56 for gasoline, P55 for diesel, and P83.47 for kerosene.
The Philippines imports much of its petroleum requirements as finished products, making domestic prices vulnerable to changes in regional fuel markets, freight costs, and foreign exchange rates.

Excise taxes on liquefied petroleum gas and kerosene have been suspended since late September, under Executive Order No. 125 issued by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. The relief does not cover gasoline or diesel. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Saudi Arabia’s influence loomed large over failed COP31 deal
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia and fellow members of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries have long opposed climate language targeting fossil fuels, saying they need to be part of the global energy…

blocks.text: Seats reserved for Saudi Arabia in the foreground as meetings continue at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, November 17, 2026. REUTERS/Umit Bektas
Umit Bektas/Reuters

Saudi Arabia and fellow members of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries have long opposed climate language targeting fossil fuels, saying they need to be part of the global energy mix for the foreseeable future

items: At COP31 in Antalya, Saudi Arabia's influence was criticized for obstructing discussions on fossil fuel reduction, leading to a lack of political agreement for the first time since 2009.
Negotiators from vulnerable nations expressed frustration over the absence of fossil fuel references in the revised draft text, which they deemed essential for addressing climate change.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

ANTALYA, Turkey – As the COP31 climate conference drifted into what proved to be record overtime, a negotiator from a small island state complained that a promised meeting with the talks’ Turkish and Australian presidents had been canceled yet again.

Saudi officials, meanwhile, had regular access, allowing them disproportionate influence at the Antalya conference, according to negotiators from Europe, small island states, Latin America, Asia and Africa.

Riyadh was at the forefront of resisting language on reducing reliance on fossil fuels, the negotiators said, adding that was chiefly why a political agreement could not be reached for the first time since 2009.

The European Union, several small island states, and other nations particularly vulnerable to climate change said they could not accept a text that failed to mention the oil, gas, and coal that scientists say drive global warming.

“This COP, I believe, was hijacked by some oil states,” Ireland’s climate minister Darragh O’Brien told Reuters on behalf of the European Union when asked about Saudi Arabia’s role in the negotiations.
The Turkish COP presidency said in a statement no group or country was given “preferential treatment.” Representatives for Saudi Arabia and Australia did not immediately comment for this story.

Saudi Arabia and fellow members of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries have long opposed climate language targeting fossil fuels, saying they need to be part of the global energy mix for the foreseeable future.
Fossil fuels were explicitly mentioned in texts from previous COPs in 2021 in Glasgow and 2023 in Dubai.

But several negotiators said Riyadh’s hand was strengthened at Antalya by the absence of active US engagement at COP31 and the lack of close US-China coordination that has helped broker compromises at previous COPs.
“Instead of having one or two major players helping define the boundaries of the discussion, those boundaries have become less clear,” Singapore Environment Minister Grace Fu said.

COP31 began with modest expectations. Host Turkey was pushing a pledge to boost global electrification, and promising to emphasize implementation of past climate deals meant to help the planet avoid the worst consequences of global warming.
But divisions deepened after the Turkish presidency released a revised draft cover text that omitted any reference to fossil fuels.

As countries spent the second week of the talks trying to forge consensus around the wide range of options, delegates and observers said Saudi Arabia kept a fixed position: the text must not mention fossil fuels, and it should include language boosting carbon capture technologies that can reduce their emissions.
One delegate from an Asian country involved in the talks said Riyadh framed the positions as non-negotiable, even existential.
Saudi Arabia was not the only side unwilling to compromise, however. The European Union also hardened its position.
When asked how talks were going on Saturday, November 21, EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said: “It’s either going to be a good deal, or it’s going to be no deal.”

Germany convened meetings with small island states and other members of the High Ambition Coalition, which groups vulnerable nations, African countries and developed countries, including Singapore and Canada.
Together they produced a letter, backed by around 130 countries, that said any deal at Antalya must include mention of transitioning away from fossil fuels, and sent it to the presidency.

Around the same time, and as Saturday slipped into Sunday, November 22, Saudi, Chinese and Russian officials frequently visited the presidency’s offices, even as representatives from other groups struggled to get meetings, delegates told Reuters.

When the revised text finally emerged early on Sunday, many countries reacted angrily. The text largely ignored the coalition letter: it still had no mention of fossil fuels and kept strong language promoting carbon capture.
“It seems like we are negotiating with the Saudis,” Maina Talia, Tuvalu’s climate minister, said at the time.

As Sunday wore on, negotiators openly discussed the possibility that the talks could collapse without achieving a political statement. Delegates were leaving Antalya to catch flights. Time was running out.
After the closing plenary started on Sunday afternoon in Antalya, COP31 president Murat Kurum said he could see there was no agreement and confirmed he would not advance any new text.

Some negotiators were left with the feeling the producers of the fossil fuels that have contributed to climate change wielded more power than those who want to accelerate the transition to a low-carbon world.
“It seems like when fossil fuels cannot be mentioned in the cover text, then somehow the oil countries have a larger voice at this COP,” said Danish Climate Minister Samira Nawa. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Break the Fake Movement to host the AI Literacy Summit 2026
articles.summary: The future of AI literacy in the Philippines is about to take another step forward at the AI Literacy Summit
articles.byline: Francis Christian Lubag, Paolo Miguel Ordonio

blocks.text: The future of AI literacy in the Philippines is about to take another step forward at the AI Literacy Summit 2026, on November 28, 2026, at the University of Santo Tomas in Manila, Philippines.

Following the successful program implementation and to celebrate our milestone along with the 2026 Global Media and Information Literacy Week, the Break the Fake Movement, in partnership with the University of Santo Tomas, organized the Summit to bring together youth, the academe, media, civil society organizations, and government institutions to dialogue about the future of AI literacy in the country.

The gathering comes on the heels of the AI Ready ASEAN Programme completion, which saw Break the Fake Movement successfully train more than 350,000 Filipinos on effective AI use and literacy. Across Southeast Asia, the program led to 9 million trained individuals.

With the theme “Continuing the Conversation on Shaping an Inclusive and Ethical AI Literacy for the Philippines,” the Summit will serve as an avenue to map AI literacy in the Philippines in light of public and private interventions over the years. Moreover, the event aims to chart a path forward for identifying core AI competencies, developing actionable strategies to integrate AI into learning and everyday practices, promoting ethical AI use, and strengthening digital resilience. Building on the outcomes and learnings from the AI Ready ASEAN Programme, the Summit aims to catalyze a multi-sectoral National AI Literacy Action Plan, directly reinforcing the country’s role as a regional leader in driving inclusive and human-centered digital innovation.

Driving the conversations are speakers and panelists from the ASEAN Foundation, the University of Santo Tomas, the AI Ready ASEAN Programme Local Implementing Partners and selected Master Trainers, the Department of Education, the Department of Information and Communications Technology, Safe AI Philippines, and MediaSmarts Canada.

Due to the limited onsite capacity, registration for in-person participation is now closed. You can still join the Summit virtually through a livestream. Follow Break the Fake Movement’s official social media page to catch the livestream of the event.
For more details about the Summit, you may contact btfm_programs@breakthefakemovement.com.

The Sandiganbayan Third Division has denied the petition for bail of Senator Rodante Marcoleta and three others who are facing a P75 million plunder charge over undeclared campaign contributions to the lawmaker.
This was confirmed by Atty. Dennis Pulma, Clerk of Court of the Sandiganbayan Third Division.
Marcoleta’s other co-accused in the case, who will also remain in detention, are former Anakalusugan party-list Rep. Mike Defensor, businessman Joseph Espiritu, and Aristotle Viray.

Based on the criminal information filed by the Ombudsman prosecutors, the donor’s tax for the said P75 million campaign donation was only paid in December 2025, an indication of concealment since the donation was already made in January 2025.

Marcoleta, in a television interview in November 2025, said that he received P75 million donation from his friends but he did not declare this as campaign expenditure because it was upon the request of the donors to become anonymous.
The senator, however, said in his position paper submitted to the Commission on Elections (Comelec) that such donation was a personal fund of his, prompting the Comelec to stop the investigation.
This difference in Marcoleta’s accounts was included in the basis of the Ombudsman’s probe and the eventual filing of charges against Marcoleta and his co-accused. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Lacson flags double funding for flood control projects in 2027 budget
articles.summary: Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson has flagged duplicate appropriations for some flood control projects in the proposed 2027 national budget, raising fresh concerns over funding irregularities amid the…

blocks.text: Published November 23, 2026 1:12pm

Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson has flagged duplicate appropriations for some flood control projects in the proposed 2027 national budget, raising fresh concerns over funding irregularities amid the ongoing controversy over anomalous flood control projects.

In a statement, Lacson said Monday he would seek the removal of duplicate or multiple allocations during the Senate's deliberations on the proposed budget and, if necessary, during the bicameral conference committee proceedings.
“We found more irregularities. Double appropriations. Not only are these flood control projects, but they have also been allocated funding twice,” he said.

The senator said the duplicate allocations were separate from at least 30 alleged ghost multipurpose buildings (MPBs) his team had identified in the proposed budget. He also intends to move for their removal.

Over the weekend, Lacson questioned the proposed appropriations for 3,950 MPBs, separate from the 1,584 MPBs covered by the Local Government Support Fund's (LGSF) Financial Assistance to local government units (LGUs) subprogram from 2022 to 2026.
He cited cases in which MPBs had received funding in previous years, including 2024, 2025 and 2026, but no structures had been built at their designated sites as of this year.
“Our team flagged at least 30 such projects in various parts of the country,” he said.
Lacson also said initial findings indicated that MPB projects involved commissions, although these were allegedly smaller than those associated with anomalous flood control projects.
He said commissions for MPBs could reach 10% of project costs. Earlier this year, Lacson cited alleged kickbacks ranging from 15% to 30% for proponents of anomalous flood control projects.
Lacson said he and his staff were continuing to scrutinize the proposed budget for questionable allocations and would seek their removal during the legislative process.

“In the Senate version, we will still have a period for amendments. If we can show our colleagues that the additional funding is unnecessary because the same project has already been allocated funds, I believe it would be right to remove it, including during the bicameral conference committee proceedings,” he said.
He added that the scrutiny had uncovered more questionable allocations, stressing that duplicate funding should be removed.
“If there are duplicate appropriations, one should definitely be removed. If there are four allocations, three should be removed,” Lacson said.

The senator's latest budget findings come amid a sweeping corruption controversy involving alleged irregularities in government flood control projects, which came to light in July 2025 after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ordered an investigation into reports of ghost and substandard infrastructure.
The controversy erupted after several flood control structures reportedly failed to protect communities from flooding despite being declared completed.

Investigations subsequently uncovered allegations of overpriced and nonexistent projects, questionable bidding processes and kickbacks involving contractors, Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) officials and several politicians.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Fewer than half in UK will pay TV licence fee within a decade, report warns
articles.summary:
Analysis for thinktank points to cycle of falling income leading to lower spending on content in ‘spiral of decline’

Fewer than half of households in Britain will pay the BBC’s licence…

blocks.text: Fewer than half of households in Britain will pay the BBC’s licence within a decade, according to analysis that warns that the broadcaster’s funding is locked in a “spiral of decline”.

With senior BBC figures concerned about the accelerating fall in licence fee sales, the independent projections also warn that the proportion of households paying the levy will further decline to less than a third by 2037-38 should the government persist with the corporation’s current funding model.

Lisa Nandy, the culture secretary, is preparing to publish proposed changes to the licence fee that will force anyone who watches a streaming service to pay it. Currently, only people who watch live TV or the BBC’s iPlayer have to pay the fee.

Projections by the respected independent media consultancy Oliver & Ohlbaum Associates point to an “unsustainable” cycle of falling income leading to lower spending on strong content that attracts audiences.

They show the BBC’s licence fee income – paid by 77% of households last year – could be worth less than half its current level in real terms by 2037-38, the next point at which the broadcaster’s funding model is renegotiated.
The BBC’s own internal licence fee income modelling is also said to be bleak, with the corporation already making painful cuts to programmes and staff.
Nandy’s proposed new funding model, which could form part of the BBC’s next 10-year charter, is expected to be published before the end of the year.

Extending the licence fee to streamers would put the BBC on a more sustainable footing. However, it will be controversial with major streamers such as Netflix, Disney, Amazon and YouTube, as well as their subscribers.
Other more radical proposals, such as a household levy for the BBC, have already been ruled out by the Treasury as politically impossible.

Like all media companies, the BBC is facing a myriad of pressures. The costs of making television have hugely increased, while the arrival of streamers and digital platforms has transformed viewing habits.
Meanwhile, freezes to the licence fee over the past decade, as well as extra costs loaded on to the BBC by previous governments, have given the corporation less to spend.
The new independent projections, included in a report on the BBC by the Reset Tech thinktank, show why the broadcaster’s leadership and ministers accept that the status quo cannot continue.

The study suggests the BBC’s spending on TV content will more than halve by the next charter review. BBC viewing per person via TV sets would fall from 46 minutes a day in 2024-25 to just 23 minutes a day in 2037-38. Revenue would fall from £3.8bn to £1.6bn in real terms.
The BBC remains the UK’s most-used media brand, reaching 94% of adults every month. However, the projections suggest YouTube could overtake BBC TV set viewing in 2032-33.

It is predicted that more than half of households will not pay the licence fee by 2033-34. Non-payment of the licence fee has already risen from about 9% of households in 2015 to about 23% last year, and the trend has been accelerating.

Dylan Sparks, the UK director at Reset Tech, said the report confirmed that the BBC’s current funding model was broken. “The BBC is critical national infrastructure and it deserves a long-term settlement that ensures it not only survives but thrives in the decades to come,” he said.
“We urge the government to defend this vital British asset and to use the BBC charter renewal process to come forward with a new funding model that is universal, affordable and sustainable.”

A BBC spokesperson said: “We have consistently argued that the current funding model is not sustainable and needs reform. We will continue to engage with government to secure a new charter that provides sufficient, sustainable and universal funding so the BBC can deliver for audiences for generations to come.”

articles.title: Sandiganbayan denies Marcoleta’s bail request in plunder case
articles.summary: This means that Marcoleta will remain detained during his trial

blocks.text: Senator Rodante Marcoleta, accompanied by PNP Criminal Investigation and Detection Group personnel, leaves the anti-graft court Sandiganbayan on July 15, 2026, and will be brought to the Quezon City Jail in Payatas.
Jire Carreon/Rappler
This means that Marcoleta will remain detained during his trial
MANILA, Philippines – The Sandiganbayan 3rd Division has denied the bail petition of Senator Rodante Marcoleta in his plunder case.
The 3rd Division justices unanimously voted to deny Marcoleta’s bail petition, which means that he will remain detained during his trial.
Plunder is a non-bailable offense. In cases like these, the accused needs to file a bail petition with the court and the prosecution will present evidence to block the bail.

The decision of the anti-graft court means the justices found that the evidence of guilt against Marcoleta is strong — the threshold of evidence required for bail petitions. This does not mean, however, that the lawmaker and his co-accused are already found guilty.
Plunder, which has a threshold of P50 million, is a corruption offense involving public officials.

The Office of the Ombudsman filed the case against Marcoleta in July, due to questions related to the P75-million campaign donations he received. Aside from plunder, the senator is also facing three counts of alleged violation of Presidential Decree No. 46 (receiving gifts).

These cases stemmed from Marcoleta’s campaign donations for his senatorial run in 2025. He declared P51 million as net worth that year, but spent P112 million for his campaign. He did not declare any poll contributions.
Later, Marcoleta himself confirmed in a television interview that he received P75 million in campaign donations, explaining that he received the money before the campaign period started.

The senator explained that he did not include this in his Statement of Contributions and Expenditures (SOCE) because he was not yet a candidate when got the money. At the time, however, he was sitting congressman.
Marcoleta has also been suspended as a senator since October 19 as plunder case carries the penalty of suspension of officials. – Rappler.com

articles.title: #CourageON: Finding community-centered climate solutions beyond COP31
articles.summary: For LILAK, real climate action should respect indigenous rights, return land control to communities, and give them a direct say over their lands and food systems

blocks.text: The 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) concluded on November 22 in Antalya, Turkey. Leaders, organizations, and advocates from around the world came together to discuss climate change and just transition, aiming to turn promises into real-world solutions.

While some groups followed the discussions from outside the conference, others chose not to participate. One of them is LILAK (Purple Action for Indigenous Women’s Rights), a collective of feminists, activists, and indigenous women advocating for indigenous women’s rights, ancestral lands, and the environment.

LILAK has always been critical of COPs and boycotted some of the previous talks even before COP31. For the group, engaging with it in the past took up too much of their resources, and they would rather invest their time and energy in indigenous communities.
Rappler spoke with members of LILAK about their advocacies and views on the climate talks.
What specific issues pushed you to not engage in the summit?

Che Polutan, LILAK’s program officer, attended the COP27 negotiations in Egypt in 2022. She said the process itself was overwhelming for communities, with no meaningful space for them, as the negotiations were corporate- and capital-driven.

In 2025, Judy Pasimio, LILAK’s overall coordinator, attended the People’s COP in Belem, Brazil. She explained that “COP should be about the Conference of Peoples, where genuine solutions are discussed.”
“However, what is being discussed [at] COP are solutions for profit,” she added.

blocks.caption: LILAK AT COP30. Judy Pasimio and Rachel Tahay, a Teduray indigenous woman, attend the People’s COP in Belém, Brazil. Photo courtesy of Judy Pasimio

blocks.text: How is the climate crisis affecting your communities, and how does that shape your current campaigns?

Food and climate have always been tied to the significant role of indigenous women as food producers and carers of their families and communities. They are primarily affected and most vulnerable not only during disasters but also in their food production and food systems.

Judy said corporate-backed “solutions” at COP, such as climate smart agriculture and green transition projects, are profit-driven schemes that affect indigenous communities. CSA uses high-tech methods, such as lab-bred seeds, chemical inputs, and automated tools, to help crops survive extreme weather, but critics argue it forces farmers to rely on expensive corporate products instead of traditional seeds. Some green transition projects, meanwhile, fuel destructive mining and deforestation, damaging local ecosystems while profits and clean energy flow to wealthy nations.
While both aim to fight climate change, Judy said these so-called solutions displace communities, cut off their access to lands and seas, and erase the role of indigenous women in food production.

“The Philippines, for one, is very strong on climate solutions and its negotiations on these platforms, but this strong stand does not translate here in our country. The government’s development plan is shaped by investments exploiting our natural resources,” she emphasized.
“It does not benefit our country.”
What critical issues are COP31 negotiators ignoring, and what does real climate action look like for indigenous women?
Che emphasized that indigenous communities are heavily impacted by the climate emergency. For her, they should be part of the discussions.
Climate disasters placed a heavy burden on indigenous women, who take on extra care work and find ways to keep their families afloat, especially before and after crises.

She criticized the COP negotiations for sidelining women’s issues, arguing that real climate action should respect indigenous rights, return land control to communities, and give them a direct say over their lands and food systems.

“It starts in recognizing and respecting their rights and supporting their indigenous knowledge, systems and practices. If we recognize these, we will be able to stop the encroachment and destruction of development industries,” she explained.
How would you distinguish actual, accountable progress from just another empty pledge?

Judy said the Philippines needs a national development plan centered on local needs rather than foreign investments. She also highlighted traditional practices such as seed banking and seed exchanges among communities as models for food sovereignty. She called for support for women- and community-led solutions rather than corporate schemes.
“Dapat ’yong mga communities ang sinusuportahan (It’s communities that should be supported).” – Rappler.com

#CourageON is a bi-monthly newsletter providing updates from our communities. In time for the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), the month of November features stories of courage and resilience from our partner communities and advocates.

articles.title: US intelligence chief predicts more tech outages as systems undergo upgrades
articles.summary: 'As part of that ongoing upgrade, we are going to have glitches, gaps, interruptions in service,' Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton tells CNN

blocks.text: 'As part of that ongoing upgrade, we are going to have glitches, gaps, interruptions in service,' Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton tells CNN

WASHINGTON, USA – Americans should expect more technology outages and disruptions as companies and government agencies replace aging systems, the top US intelligence official said on Sunday, November 22.

“And as part of that ongoing upgrade, we are going to have glitches, gaps, interruptions in service,” Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNN’s “State of the Union” program. “That is going to happen.”

Clayton was interviewed on Sunday morning news programs days after President Donald Trump attributed a recent spate of technology failures to upgrades of companies’ technology systems. Clayton said the upgrades were necessary to improve performance and cybersecurity as technological advances strain older systems.

A string of technology failures this month disrupted critical US systems, including a nationwide halt to air travel, a Microsoft outage that hit email services, a technical glitch that affected several major banks and a temporary disruption to the National Security Agency’s network.

blocks.caption: Trump ousts cyber director after tech outages spark criticism

blocks.text: Speaking on the ABC program “This Week,” Clayton reiterated his previous statements that those outages were not the result of coordinated or state-sponsored actions, attributing them to technical upgrades.
Clayton declined to discuss specifics of separate reports of cyberattacks on the FBI and Department of Agriculture, saying he expects investigators to provide answers “in due course.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Ombudsman seeks to drop Samchan exec from Romualdez plunder case
articles.summary: Ombudsman prosecutors have asked the Sandiganbayan to drop an executive of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp. as a co-accused in the P7.4-billion plunder case against former House Speaker and Leyte Rep.…

blocks.text: Published November 23, 2026 12:35pm

Ombudsman prosecutors have asked the Sandiganbayan to drop an executive of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp. as a co-accused in the P7.4-billion plunder case against former House Speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez over their alleged involvement in the flood control kickback scheme.

The request to exclude Samchan executive Felicito Guevarra was contained in an omnibus motion filed by the Ombudsman before the Sandiganbayan Third Division. Its chairperson, Associate Justice Karl Miranda, announced the motion ahead of Romualdez's bail hearing on Monday, Nov. 23.

Aside from seeking Guevarra's exclusion from the list of accused, prosecutors asked the court to allow him to testify during Romualdez's bail hearing in place of former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan. They also sought Guevarra's continued detention at the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) facility.
Guevarra surrendered to the NBI on Nov. 19.

Deputy Special Prosecutor Omar Sagadal said the proposed amendment to the criminal information and Guevarra's presentation as a witness were justified under Section 14, Rule 110 of the Rules of Criminal Procedure, which allows amendments to charges provided they are not substantial.
“The good cause is apparent. It (Guevarra’s surrender) is something not within our control, Your Honors. It is also a surprise to us,” Sagadal said.
“The amendment of the information does not change the theory of the prosecution. It does maintain conspiracy. It does maintain plunder,” he added.
Other accused in the plunder case include former House appropriations committee chairperson Zaldy Co of the Ako Bicol party-list and Jocelyn Sereño, a staff member of Romualdez.
Samchan has been implicated in the alleged movement and laundering of proceeds from the flood control kickback scheme.

During Romualdez's bail hearing, an Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) investigator testified that Samchan purchased a P294.23-million manager's check used by Golden Pheasant Holdings Corp., an alleged dummy company linked to Romualdez, to acquire a property in Forbes Park, Makati City.

The AMLC also traced 21 check deposits totaling P1.72 billion, made between March 10 and 27, 2023, to an account reportedly belonging to Samchan. The funds were linked to transactions involving the property acquisition, the investigator said.

The Ombudsman had accused Samchan of knowingly facilitating or aiding the alleged laundering of proceeds from unlawful activities. The company also returned earnings from flagged transactions to the Bureau of the Treasury, according to the Ombudsman.

Romualdez's lawyer, Raschel Pomoy, opposed the prosecution's omnibus motion, arguing that introducing another witness when prosecutors were scheduled to conclude their presentation of evidence on Nov. 24 would unfairly prejudice her client.

The Sandiganbayan said it would resolve the Ombudsman's motion as soon as possible. It also set Dec. 4 as the final day for the presentation of prosecution witnesses in Romualdez's bail hearing.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: ‘Difficult geopolitical times’: Albanese defends Bowen after Cop31 deal failure
articles.summary: Coalition calls for climate change minister to resign immediately or be sacked over ‘catastrophic diplomatic disaster’, despite offering no alternatives on reducing emissions
articles.byline: Graham Readfearn in Antalya and Josh Butler in Canberra

blocks.text: Anthony Albanese has defended Chris Bowen from criticism following the failure of the UN Cop31 climate summit, blaming the result on “difficult geopolitical times” as the Coalition called for the minister to resign.
Bowen served as president of negotiations at the talks in Turkey, helping run the conference with his Turkish counterpart, Murat Kurum.

Speaking to journalists late on Sunday after a list of countries rejected a proposed “cover decision” – an overarching agreement – for the conference, Bowen said “Australia left nothing on the field” but the “red lines” he and his staff tried to negotiate to find consensus between nearly 200 countries were unbridgeable.

The biggest sticking point was whether the agreement would mention the need for the world to transition away from fossil fuels. The European Union, Panama, the Marshall Islands, Vanuatu, Norway and Belize told the conference they would not accept a deal without it.
Saudi Arabia and Russia led a group of oil-rich countries that vowed to veto a decision that included mention of fossil fuels.
Bowen told reporters: “I would have been happy with [a] transition away from fossil fuels being in the text, but that was not going to get support.”

He said despite the breakdown, “in the real world” the transition away from fossil fuels was inevitable and happening at speed. He said more than 90 countries had signed a pledge to increase electrification to 35% by 2035 – a step that should help cut fossil fuel use if delivered – but acknowledged the result was “very disappointing”.

Australia was sharply criticised during the conference for its continued support for new coal and gas export developments. Speaking on Monday, Albanese said Australia’s efforts had been critical in building relationships with Pacific neighbours.

“It’s evidence that we’re living in difficult geopolitical times,” he said of the result. “That is the reality. The important work of Cop is the work that we’ve done with the Pacific, where Australia and our Pacific leaders have worked constructively together.
“In order to have credibility [in the Pacific], the entry fee is action on climate change.”
The Coalition’s energy spokesperson, Dan Tehan, said Bowen should “resign immediately”.

“If Chris Bowen does not resign immediately, the prime minister should sack him,” Tehan said. “As the lead negotiator, Chris Bowen is personally responsible for this catastrophic diplomatic disaster.”

The Greens’ deputy leader, Steph Hodgins-May, said it was a “disastrous embarrassment” that Australia had chaired negotiations over the failed deal. In a statement, she said Labor was “not fit to lead – not on the world stage for climate negotiations, and not at home when it comes to protecting Australians from climate destruction”.

The Coalition, and Tehan specifically, have consistently attacked Labor’s bid to host the conference and Bowen’s installation as president of negotiations. Bowen argued for the role – newly created for Cop31 – after Turkey won the hosting rights after a protracted stand0ff.

Tehan did not say what the Coalition would have done differently if he was in Bowen’s shoes, other than saying the opposition would not have pursued hosting Cop or the position of president of negotiations. The Coalition has abandoned its support for Australia reaching net zero emissions by 2050 – a target introduced under former Liberal prime minister Scott Morrison – and promised to abolish Labor’s climate policies if elected.
It has not put forward any policies to reduce emissions.
Tehan said the consensus model of agreement used at the UN summit was “completely and utterly broken”. “Chris Bowen should have known that,” he said.
after newsletter promotion
While the failure to get countries to agree to the “Antalya pact” in Turkey was a significant moment in the history of UN climate summits, the talks did not collapse completely.
The sticking point was the attempt to find language to reflect the “transition away for fossil fuels” that had been agreed to in 2023 in Dubai.
In the final stages of the talks, countries were presented with a text that only referred back to that decision and did not explicitly say “fossil fuels” – infuriating a sweep of countries.

Bill Hare, the Australian chief executive of Climate Analytics and a Cop veteran, said the lack of agreement on the main document at Cop31 – there was consensus on some minor issues – should not be seen as a failure of the entire Cop process but as “a successful defence of the [UN climate convention’s] integrity against a coordinated attack by a few countries implacably opposed to action on climate change, in particular to any mention of the need to transition away from fossil fuels”.

Amanda Cahill, founder of the Next Economy, was in Antalya to offer advice on elements of the conference dealing with the so-called “just transition” – a wide-reaching set of guidelines meant to protect communities and workers affected by climate change and the shift away from the fossil fuel industry.
“While we didn’t get the outcome we wanted at this Cop, we maintained the global commitment to justice and equity as countries transition their economies to deal with climate change,” she said.

“We’ve got a lot of work ahead of us, but parties have committed to ensuring the Just Transition Mechanism is set up and that countries can get the support they need to implement meaningful and just climate action.”

Adam Bandt, the former Greens leader and chief executive of the Australian Conservation Foundation, said countries had “understandably” rejected a pact that he said “failed to even mention the main causes of the climate crisis, let alone address them”.
“The prime minister’s snub of the UN secretary general by failing to mention coal and gas in his speech set the tone early in this summit,” he said.

articles.title: Israel’s destruction of Gaza has created a ‘toxic wasteland’, experts find
articles.summary:
Scientific and satellite findings warn of widespread contamination in Gaza, posing grave threats to public health ‘for generations to come’

Israel’s destruction of Gaza has left a…

blocks.text: Israel’s destruction of Gaza has left a devastating environmental legacy with poisoned water, contaminated soil and toxic air threatening the life-support systems that the population depends on for survival, according to a report.

Israel’s military assault has created widespread contamination across the entire strip, the report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory (Ceobs) finds, with heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings, and sewage making the air, soil and water dangerous for Palestinians for decades to come.

Oxfam International’s executive director, Amitabh Behar, said: “Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza includes military assaults on its environment, which are environmental war crimes threatening life now and for generations to come.”

He said the “destruction and contamination of Gaza” have “fundamentally degraded the environmental conditions necessary for human safety and survival” and breach Israel’s legal obligations under international humanitarian and human rights law.

“Palestinians living in Gaza are being exposed to toxins … through air, food, water and via direct contact with contaminated soils and debris. These risks will persist for generations to come, unless clean-up, remediation and recovery actions are prioritised.”

blocks.caption: Land bulldozed by Israeli forces near the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza last week. Photograph: Omar Ashtawy/HL/Getty

blocks.text: In 2025 and earlier this year, the UN independent international commission of inquiry found that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza and that Israeli officials, including the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, incited these acts. The Israeli mission in Geneva said Israel rejected the commission’s “libellous sham”. Netanyahu is separately wanted by the international criminal court (ICC) for war crimes.

Oxfam’s report gives the most comprehensive picture to date of what it calls the “toxic wasteland” created by the Israeli assault which has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians and wounded at least 175,000, while thousands still remain unaccounted for under the rubble.

Using satellite imagery, remote sensing, scientific analysis and other open-source data, it concludes contamination in Gaza is “widespread, severe and consequential, with serious implications for public health and civilian survival”.

Behar said: “It is horrifying to begin to understand the extent of toxic contamination being faced by the population, who can neither escape nor protect themselves properly from the dangers. In an area as small, oppressed and densely populated as Gaza, continuous exposure is inevitable, with people surrounded by waste and sewage, spreading pests and the risk of disease growing.
“Raw sewage is pouring into the sea and leaking into the ground, while the destruction of Gaza’s sanitation systems leaves people with little protection from the contamination around them.”

blocks.caption: Displaced Palestinians living near a rubbish-filled sewage waste flow in Gaza City. The destruction of sanitation systems leaves people with little protection from contamination. Photograph: Ahmad Hasaballah/Getty

blocks.text: He added the “associated health consequences will be severe, with children and pregnant women among those facing the highest risks”.

The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) estimates that Israel’s military operations have generated more than 61m tonnes of debris across the territory, turning Gaza’s destroyed homes, neighbourhoods and infrastructure into a vast reservoir of potentially hazardous materials.

The report’s author, Lama Abdul Samad, a global water and sanitation specialist at Oxfam, said tackling the environmental damage in Gaza will be “highly challenging because contamination is dispersed across the urban rubble, farmland, water systems and soils, while unexploded ordnance continues to restrict safe access to most areas”.

blocks.caption: Children walk past an unexploded missile at a Gaza City rubbish dump. Photograph: Majdi Fathi/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

blocks.text: “The analysis highlights the urgent need for Israel to grant access for a detailed environmental assessment on the ground to clarify the risks to public health and identify options for urgent harm-reduction measures. Restoration is likely to require extensive clearance, monitoring and specialised remediation of affected areas from contaminants such as explosive residues, organic pollutants and heavy metals.”
Behar said that as international attention increasingly turned to Gaza’s reconstruction, environmental recovery must not be treated as an afterthought, but as a vital undertaking in parallel.
“Rebuilding Gaza without simultaneously understanding and addressing the extent of environmental contamination risks creating long-term public health consequences for generations to come,” he said.
The Israeli government has been contacted for comment.

articles.title: November 23: 2 areas under ‘danger’ heat index — PAGASA

Philstar.com illustration
MANILA, Philippines — Two areas in Luzon could be placed under the “danger” heat index classification on Monday, November 23, the state weather bureau PAGASA said.
In its weather forecast, Coron and Cuyo in Palawan were listed among the areas expected to experience temperatures that could cause heat cramps or heat stroke with prolonged exposure.
According to PAGASA, Cuyo may experience a heat index of up to 43°Celsius., while Coron may reach 42°C.
Meanwhile, most parts of the country are forecast to remain under the “extreme caution” category, with heat index levels ranging from 33°C to 41°C.

In Metro Manila, the Science Garden station in Quezon City is expected to record a heat index of 37°C, while the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) station in Pasay City could reach 39°C. Both fall under the extreme caution category.
The elevated heat index readings come as the country experiences a very strong El Niño, despite the presence of the northeast monsoon, locally known as amihan.

articles.title: 'No Zalameda Court': Chief Justice vows to uphold judicial integrity
articles.summary: Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda vowed on Monday to uphold integrity and independence in the judiciary as he began his tenure as the new head of the Supreme Court (SC).

blocks.text: Published November 23, 2026 11:42am
Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda vowed on Monday to uphold integrity and independence in the judiciary as he began his tenure as the new head of the Supreme Court (SC).
Speaking at his first flag-raising ceremony, Zalameda stressed that under his leadership, there would be no “Zalameda Court,” but only a judiciary that answers to the people.
“To my colleagues, I am here to work with and for the Court. The way I see it, I am simply its humble representative,” Zalameda said.
“There is no Zalameda Court. There is only the Supreme Court of the Philippines, comprising us all, answering only to the people,” he added.
He said the occasion was meaningful as it gave him his first opportunity to address SC personnel in his capacity as Chief Justice.

“Gusto ko pong magpasalamat sa inyong pagtanggap sa akin (I would like to thank you for welcoming me). Let us carry forward our shared commitment to integrity and service in everything we do,” Zalameda said.
Zalameda said he accepted the responsibility entrusted to him with “humility, independence, and determination,” pledging to serve as a “servant of justice” until his last day in office.
Judges' safety

Recalling the killing of Basilan Judge Joseph Wee Sit, Zalameda said the tragedy underscored the dangers faced by judges and court personnel but stressed that threats would not deter the judiciary from fulfilling its mandate.

“This tragedy is a sobering reminder of the very real dangers facing our judges and court personnel. Nakakalungkot po talaga (It's truly saddening). But stronger than our grief and outrage is our shared resolve. No threats will ever shutter our courts or silence the pursuit of justice,” he said.
He assured judges and court personnel that the SC would prioritize their safety and protect their independence.
“To our judges and court personnel, hindi kayo pababayaan ng Korte Suprema. Gagawin namin ang lahat upang matiyak ang inyong kaligtasan at mapangalagaan ang inyong kalayaan,” Zalameda said.
(To our judges and court personnel, the Supreme Court will not abandon you. We will do everything to ensure your safety and protect your independence.)
He also called on members of the justice sector to unite in protecting the judiciary's ability to deliver justice.
Zalameda took his oath on Nov. 6 as the Philippines' 28th Chief Justice, succeeding retired Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Manchester’s Co-op Live arena evacuated after apparent tear gas incident at Don Toliver concert
articles.summary:
Incident occurred near the end of Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver, with one person taken to hospital

Police have evacuated

blocks.text: Police have evacuated Manchester’s Co-op Live arena after a substance believed to be teargas was let off in the crowd during a Don Toliver concert.
Greater Manchester police said the incident occurred near the end of the US rapper’s show on Sunday evening.

Greater Manchester police said concertgoers had been safely evacuated, with several people being assessed on site for side effects as a precaution and inquiries under way to determine what the substance was. No serious injuries have been reported.
Assistant chief constable Steph Parker said in a statement: “Our priority was to ensure the safety of every person that was attending the concert.
“Several people were treated on site, and one has been taken to hospital at this time. Anyone who has left the event and since become unwell is advised to attend their local hospital.
“We understand the concern that this incident will have raised – particularly those with loved ones at the venue last night – and we’d like to thank everyone for their patience as we dealt with it.
“There were over 12,000 people in attendance during this concert who were safely escorted from the arena so they could make their way home.”
She continued: “Our declaration of a major incident has allowed us to ensure emergency services and partner agencies can work together quickly and effectively to coordinate a safe response.
“We will now begin to fully understand what this substance was and how this incident came about.”
The north-west ambulance service said one person was taken to hospital and more than 50 were assessed by clinicians.
The service said in a statement: “We deployed several emergency crews, including our Hazardous Area Response Team, to support the safe assessment and treatment of people at the scene.

“More than 50 people have been assessed by our clinicians, with some reporting eye and respiratory symptoms. Decontamination is being carried out as a precaution and one patient has been taken to Manchester Royal Infirmary for further assessment.

“The incident remains ongoing and our teams remain at the scene assessing and caring for patients. We continue to work closely with emergency service partners while inquiries are carried out to establish what the substance was.
“Anyone at tonight’s event who has since noticed side effects or become ill should seek medical advice.”
Footage shared on social media appeared to show concertgoers coughing and covering their mouths as they left the venue.
Co-op Live has the capacity to hold 23,500 people, with American singer Phoebe Bridgers scheduled to perform at the venue on Thursday.
Don Toliver is partway through the UK leg of his Octane World Tour.

articles.title: Zalameda urges CA to act on Maguindanao massacre appeals
articles.summary: Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda on Monday urged the Court of Appeals (CA) to promptly resolve the pending appeals in the Maguindanao massacre case, as the country marked the 17th anniversary of the…

blocks.text: Published November 23, 2026 11:23am

Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda on Monday urged the Court of Appeals (CA) to promptly resolve the pending appeals in the Maguindanao massacre case, as the country marked the 17th anniversary of the tragedy.

Speaking at his first flag-raising ceremony as Chief Justice, Zalameda said the victims and their families had waited long enough for justice, stressing that the proceedings should no longer be delayed.

“As we speak of protecting those who stand for justice, we must also remember the victims of the Ampatuan Massacre, whose 17th anniversary we commemorate today. The victims and their families have waited long enough,” Zalameda said.

“I therefore urge the Court of Appeals to resolve the pending appeals with dispatch, consistent with due process and rights of all parties. Let us ensure that justice is not delayed any further,” he added.

The Maguindanao massacre, also known as the Ampatuan massacre, took place on Nov. 23, 2009, when a convoy carrying relatives and supporters of then Buluan Vice Mayor Esmael Mangudadatu, along with journalists and other civilians, was ambushed in Ampatuan town, Maguindanao.

The victims were accompanying Mangudadatu’s wife, Genalyn, and other family members as they were on their way to file his certificate of candidacy for the 2010 gubernatorial elections. Fifty-seven people were killed in the attack, including 32 journalists and media workers, making it the deadliest single attack on journalists in history.
The family of photojournalist Reynaldo “Bebot” Momay, whose remains were never recovered, continues to seek his recognition as the 58th victim of the massacre.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Video of ICE detaining father and daughter while boarding flight sparks protests in Seattle
articles.summary:
Footage of Saturday incident, filmed by fellow passengers, quickly went viral on social media as mayor calls tactics ‘un-American’

Protesters marched through the Seattle-Tacoma international…

blocks.text: Protesters marched through the Seattle-Tacoma international airport on Sunday after widely shared footage captured masked immigration agents detaining a father and daughter on an airport jet bridge as they boarded their Alaska Airlines flight.

Video of the incident on Saturday – filmed by fellow passengers – quickly went viral on social media, sparking condemnation from lawmakers, including Washington Democratic governor Bob Ferguson and Seattle mayor Katie Wilson.

Footage and photographs showed protesters with bullhorns and signs that read “ICE out of Washington” and “Abolish ICE” at the Seattle airport. Protesters could be seen walking inside and around the airport chanting “ICE out now” and other rallying cries.

“I made my view very clear to Alaska Airlines: They need to call on ICE to get out of our airports,” Ferguson said in a briefing. “I’ll be making that request of every other airline that operates at SeaTac airport as well.”

On Sunday a lawyer representing Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza and his daughter, Sofia Hernandez Mejia, said they were heading to a family baptism ceremony in California when they were detained by masked agents.

blocks.caption: Protesters at the Seattle airport after US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers arrested two people boarding an Alaska Airlines flight. Photograph: David Ryder/Reuters

blocks.text: Other passengers boarding the Alaska Airlines flight at Seattle-Tacoma international airport used their cellphones to film the father and daughter being detained by the officers, who were wearing unmarked jackets and khaki pants.
The videos show the officers struggling with someone on the ground. The flight, bound for Los Angeles, was delayed.

ICE has stepped up operations at airports since the summer as the agency has shifted tactics from sweeping urban raids to more targeted operations in all corners of US, with arrests reaching record levels.
Ferguson called ICE’s tactics “deeply un-American” and called for the agency’s abolition.
“The video is horrific and it is chilling,” Ferguson said at a news conference on Saturday with labor leaders and local elected officials.
Wilson called ICE’s tactics “unacceptable and un-American”.
In a statement to the Guardian, ICE said its officers detained Mendoza, an immigrant from Mexico, who it said had overstayed his visa “in violation of our nation’s laws”.

According to the ICE statement, Mejia “hurled hot coffee on the officers”. ICE said she was in the US illegally from Mexico and had overstayed her visa. She could be charged with assaulting a federal officer.

The father and daughter were travelling to attend a baptism and were seeking asylum in the US, where they had lived since 2015, their lawyer, Olia Catala, told the Associated Press. They had no criminal record, Catala said.

Mejia, who is in her mid-20s, had married a US citizen and filed paperwork for adjustment of her status, the attorney said. Mejia’s husband – who was not detained -was accompanying Mejia and her father when they were detained on Saturday, Catala added.

“They’ve done everything correctly, and these are educated people,” Catala said of the father and daughter. “She went to college, to university, she worked for a nonprofit. No criminal history [for] any of them. So it’s just heartbreaking.”

blocks.caption: A man argues with a police officer during a protest at the Seattle-Tacoma international airport. Photograph: David Ryder/Reuters

blocks.text: Both were being held at the Northwest ICE Processing Center in Tacoma, Catala said.
She said Mejia was carrying a cup of coffee when the confrontation occurred. “When somebody’s charging at you, you’re going to drop a cup of coffee,” Catala said.

“It was just a lot of commotion, and honestly, if somebody is running at you or charging at you and they’re not wearing a uniform, you don’t know who they are,” Catala said. “There was a lot of panic, chaos, not knowing what’s going on.”

Alaska Airlines said ICE officers gave no advance notice of the enforcement action, which occurred during a busy travel weekend ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. The airline said it was working with the Port of Seattle, which manages the airport, to see if protocols were followed, and had raised concerns “directly with the appropriate authorities”.

The Port of Seattle said in a statement that the arrest was distressing not only for the family but for other passengers, and that local authorities would “engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred”.
The Associated Press contributed reporting

articles.title: Boy, 7, pulled alive from rubble hours after Russian strike on Ukraine, rescuers say
articles.summary: Nine people are dead in the attack, with rescue efforts ongoing to find those still missing from the residential building.

blocks.text: A seven-year-old boy has been rescued from the rubble of a residential building in Dymer after 14 hours, in overnight Russian strikes on Dymer, in the Kyiv region, that killed nine people, Ukrainian officials have said.
The attack occurred in the early hours of Sunday. A 79-year-old woman was also rescued alive from the collapsed building, Kyiv's regional head Tymur Tkachenko said.
A strike on a private home in Bila Tserkva killed one more person and set the building ablaze, he added.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky also said three people were killed and 13 wounded in a separate strike on Vyshneve, also in the Kyiv region, that hit a grocery store on Sunday.
Ukrainian authorities said the boy in Dymer is in stable condition and was taken to hospital, and have thanked everyone involved in saving his life.
Zelensky and Ukraine's national police also confirmed the rescue of the boy.
Response teams including police, explosive technicians, dog handlers and medics are continuing with rescue efforts.
In a telegram post, Tkachenko said the 79-year-old woman rescued from the rubble was receiving treatment in hospital.
Earlier he said six people were injured in the attack, while others were still missing.

articles.title: Carney, opposition leaders trade comedic jabs at press gallery dinner
articles.summary: Two Mark Carneys and a Donald Trump shared the stage at the Parliamentary Press Gallery dinner Saturday, when the prime minister got a little help from This Hour Has 22 Minutes impersonators to give…

blocks.text: Politics·New

Two Mark Carneys and a Donald Trump shared the stage at the Parliamentary Press Gallery dinner Saturday, when the prime minister got a little help from This Hour Has 22 Minutes impersonators to give the traditional comedic speech.
'This is a tough room ... and I've been in the Oval Office,' PM jokes
FULL SPEECH | Carney roasts opposition, Trump at press gallery dinner
"I am pressing the emergency comedy button," Carney said as comedian Mark McKinney came out to perform his Carney impression on stage, before comedian Mark Critch joined with his Trump impersonation.
But Carney delivered plenty of zingers of his own in his speech, taking aim at Canadian media, his fellow party leaders, Ontario Premier Doug Ford and Trump.
"This is a tough room. And I've been in the Oval Office. Alone. With its new interior decorator," he said.

The dinner is an annual event organized by the Parliamentary Press Gallery and is attended by journalists, politicians and lobbyists. Party leaders try their hand at comedy, giving self-deprecating speeches in which they also poke fun at each other.

Carney made fun of his remarks from last week in which he was asked about Quebecor's proposal to acquire Telus. He'd answered that under certain circumstances and depending on the market structure, an oligopoly situation can lead to more competition.

"My staff are going to hate me for this, but this reminds me of a good oligopoly joke that I heard the other day. All the telcos told it to me at the same time," he said. "Look, there are market structures in which that actually would be funny."
This year, Gov. Gen. Louise Arbour also gave a speech that garnered many laughs and applause. The speech included a joke about Carney's extensive international travel.

"Our prime minister is already getting a lot of attention. Actually, I heard a guy the other day compare him to God. Now seriously, do you know the difference between God and Mark Carney? God is everywhere, and Mark Carney is everywhere except in Ottawa where he's supposed to be," she said.
Arbour also said Carney "should continue to do the wonderful job he's doing on homelessness, particularly his inspiring initiative on 24 Sussex."
She added: "And of course, he should continue the very impactful work he's doing on the environment, especially in Alberta."

The party leaders often stay for the full duration of the dinner event, but this year Carney arrived in time for his speech and headed for the door right afterward. After the journalist emcees called him out on stage for leaving, Carney watched Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre's speech from the back of the room, before exiting.
'He's stealing all my ideas'
Poilievre, who only attended for part of the evening last year, stayed for the whole event Saturday.

"Some say that Mark has a controlling leadership style. There's been reports that he yells and micromanages his staff. He acts like a miserable prick to journalists. And when I hear things like that, I say once again, he's stealing all my ideas," Poilievre said.
Poilievre ended his speech by taking aim at Liberal government funding to support journalism, bringing a bag of money on stage and pretending to hand out cash to journalists.

"I'm taking the Liberal approach. I have a special gift to help with my new media strategy. I've got a media bailout for you all. Here we go. Here's some for the Globe and Mail. Here's some for the CBC," he said.
Bloc Quebecois Leader Yves-Francois Blanchet used part of his speech to strike a serious tone, and recognize journalists' work, saying that without independent journalism there is no democracy.
NDP Leader Avi Lewis took aim at Carney's early exit. "I do not have a seat in the House of Commons, but when I am given one at dinner, I stay there all night long," he said.

He also harkened back to his previous career as a CBC host. "Back then, I was a member of the media class on the outside, looking in at the powerful. Now I'm the leader of the NDP. On the outside, looking in at the powerful," he said.
Lewis had a big act to follow, after then-interim NDP leader Don Davies gave a self-deprecating speech last year that was widely viewed as the funniest of the night.
Newly-elected Green Party Leader Mike Morrice closed off the evening, poking at Lewis and Poilievre, who lost his Carleton riding in the last federal election.
"I'm now the leader of a federal political party, having not won my own riding in 2025. But I've heard that's not a problem, right, Pierre? Avi? We're good," he joked.

articles.title: Visayas grid under red, yellow alerts on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026
articles.summary: Power interruptions are expected as the Visayas Grid will be placed under red and yellow alert on Monday, November 23, the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) said.

blocks.text: Published November 23, 2026 9:49am
Power interruptions are expected as the Visayas Grid will be placed under red and yellow alert on Monday, November 23, the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) said.
In an advisory, the NGCP said that red alert will take place from 5 p.m. to 6 p.m.
Meanwhile, the yellow alert will take effect from 3 p.m. to 5 p.m., and 6 p.m. to 8 p.m.
The red and yellow alert declarations are due to outages in several power plants in the Visayas, the grid operator said.
There will be an unplanned outage of Therma Visayas Inc. (TVI) Unit 2, while the TVI Unit 2 is running on derated capacity.
There is also a planned outage of a Palm Concepcion Power Corporation and KEPCO SPC Power Corporation Unit 2.
Further, power import from Mindanao remained limited due to the unavailability of GNPower Kauswagan Unit 3, STEAG Unit 2, and FDC Unit 3 - which are all on planned outage.

Meanwhile, eight plants are on forced outage in November, one plant since October, two plants since September, two plants since August, one plant since June, three plants since 2025, one plant since 2024, two plants since 2023, and one plant since 2021. There are also 21 plants running on derated capacities, for a total of 612.5MW unavailable to the grid.
A red alert status is issued when power supply is insufficient to meet consumer demand and the transmission grid's regulating requirement.
Meanwhile, a yellow alert is issued when the operating margin is insufficient to meet the transmission grid’s contingency requirement.
To address the thinning energy reserves in the Visayas grid, the Department of Energy (DOE) earlierorderedthe NGCP to install over 250 megawatts of battery energy storage system.
The Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) also earlier issued 24 show-cause orders (SCO) against 13 power generation companies over power outages that hit the Visayas and Mindanao. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon ‘executed’ Jesse Baird and Luke Davies then lied about it, prosecution argues
articles.summary:
Crown urges jury to reject accused’s claim of self-defence and find him guilty of murdering Sydney couple

Beau Lamarre-Condon is a “proven and persistent liar” and the evidence in his double…

blocks.text: Beau Lamarre-Condon is a “proven and persistent liar” and the evidence in his double murder trial shows the deaths of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies could only have been an “execution”, a court has been told.
Lamarre-Condon is accused of fatally shooting the Sydney couple with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
The former officer has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter, claiming the two men died while he acted in “self-defence”.
Crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC urged the jury to reject Lamarre-Condon’s account and convict him on all three counts, as he wrapped up his closing statement on Monday.

Driven by his jealous obsession, the accused drove to Paddington in a hired car, waited for his opportunity, entered the house with a gun loaded with stolen bullets, and shot Baird in the back and temple, Hatfield alleged.
“It was not self-defence or an accident,” he told the New South Wales supreme court.
“The evidence speaks only to an execution.”
Lamarre-Condon had testified he shot Baird after he lunged at him with a knife.
During this struggle, his gun was then flung across the room and picked up by Davies before the officer grabbed his arm and pushed the gun towards Davies.
Davies then pulled the trigger and shot himself, Lamarre-Condon told the court.
But this defence rests entirely on his own account and even if Baird had picked up a knife, it would not have assisted him against a glock, Hatfield said.
“You might think he is a proven and persistent liar and such a scenario is completely contrary to the weight of the evidence,” he told the court.
“The accused’s account is not the truth. It is a story made up after the fact in an attempt to meet the evidence.”
The trial before Justice Natalie Adams continues.

articles.title: US army to blow up bomb-making chemicals despite safety concerns
articles.summary:
Army invokes emergency provisions in Iowa to avoid court order despite worries about health and environment risks

The US army plans to invoke emergency provisions to avoid a court order that…

blocks.text: The US army plans to invoke emergency provisions to avoid a court order that had put on hold plans to detonate several tons of bomb-making chemicals in Iowa, saying that continued delays will make it more dangerous as the weather starts to turn colder.

“To protect its personnel and the surrounding communities, the Army needs to take swift action,” government lawyers told the eight US circuit court of appeals in a filing late on Saturday. “Protection of human health and the environment demand action now, not delay.”
The army plans to detonate the chemicals by Tuesday.
Environmental groups criticized the government’s move, decrying it as a maneuver to get around a court order and avoid public demands for safety and transparency.

The appeals court on Thursday granted a request by environmentalists to put on hold a permit that cleared the way for the detonation in Middletown, a small community about 160 miles (257km) south-east of Des Moines. It was initially planned for Friday, but the army later announced that it would push the operation to Monday after an outpouring of public concern about potential health and environmental effects.
Environmentalists have called for a review of the emergency permit that was approved earlier this month by the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).
In a statement on Sunday, the Iowa Environmental Council, Sierra Club and Earthjustice questioned claims that all alternatives were given appropriate consideration.

“The Army seemed more concerned over the weekend with finding a way to sidestep the judicial process than on meeting the public’s demands for greater transparency, notice to affected communities, and far stronger protection of people, property, and the environment from serious harm,” said Thien Chau, an attorney at Earthjustice.
Government lawyers said the army doesn’t need a permit to take emergency action against an immediate threat from explosive material.

They said the standards of a federal law regulating hazardous waste don’t apply in situations when there is an immediate threat to health, safety or the environment as determined by an explosive or munitions emergency response specialist.

Officials contend that the chemicals are unstable, and the risk of an uncontrolled explosion is growing, particularly as temperatures drop. They said there is a risk that the chemicals may explode as temperatures are expected to drop below 30F (-1C) in the coming days.

In March, staff at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant found several dozen barrels of degraded lead azide, which is used in munitions production. Crystallization of the material created an unstable and dangerous situation, prompting the army to assemble experts in munitions chemistry, engineering and environmental safety to come up with a plan.

According to EPA documents, alternatives such as neutralizing and decomposing the drums’ contents with other chemicals were considered. But officials said handling the drums would increase the probability of an accidental, fatal detonation.
The environmental groups disagreed, arguing in their petition that other alternatives were not fully considered. They also criticized officials for not sharing more information with the public.
Nearly 400 people live in Middletown, but thousands more in surrounding areas could be affected by detonated material that could disperse in the air and land on the ground.
Iowans in the region were told to stay inside, keep windows and doors closed, bring pets and livestock indoors, and clean cars, windowsills and outdoor surfaces after.
“The detonation will result in an air plume with some lead-containing particles which will disperse in the air and deposit on the ground,” an advisory states. “Lead is toxic to humans and animals.”

articles.title: Trump hosts third crypto gala for meme coin amid conflict of interest outcry
articles.summary:
Virginia dinner comes as Democrats accuse president of improperly profiting from his cryptocurrency ventures

Donald Trump is…

blocks.text: Donald Trump is scheduled to headline his third cryptocurrency gala on ⁠Sunday night at his ​country club in Virginia, rewarding top holders of his own meme coin as Democrats accuse the president of improperly profiting from his crypto ventures.

The dinner, set to take place at the Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia, will include meet-and-greets with Trump supporters including the boxing champion Floyd Mayweather, Shark Tank investor Kevin O’Leary, NBA champion Tristan Thompson and mentalist Lior Suchard, according to the event’s website.

The gala’s access and perks are divided by tiers for the 185 holders of $TRUMP, the president’s meme coin. A Trump fragrance, a poster, a “commemorative” ticket, and a “Trump watch” are reserved for 120 attendees. Meanwhile, the top 29 investors are invited to a VIP reception, and the top four will receive a “TRUMP 18K Gold Watch”.

Trump has hosted two similar galas since he took office last year, bringing a flurry of criticism as Democrats accuse Trump and his family of monetizing his brand through an array of equities and crypto ventures while in office.

blocks.caption: A statue of Donald Trump holding a bitcoin in recognition of his support for cryptocurrency is displayed on the National Mall in September 2025 in Washington DC. Photograph: Alex Brandon/AP

blocks.text: After sweepingwins in the midterms, Democrats have vowed to investigate conflicts of interest involving Trump and his personal wealth during his presidency. They also say they plan to push for legislation that would ban activities such as the meme coin gala dinner.

“This dinner and scoring mechanism appear carefully constructed to increase investment in $TRUMP, allowing the President to abuse the power of his office to personally enrich himself, as he has throughout this term,” reads a letter sent by Adam Schiff and eight other US senators last month.

Since returning to the White House, Trump has made more than $1bn from his crypto businesses, according to financial disclosures released in June. Trump received more than $500m from his World Liberty Financial business selling new crypto products, and raked another $600m from sales of souvenir-type “meme” coins stamped with Trump’s face. Trump launched his $Trump meme coin days before his inauguration.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Interest in the $TRUMP coin dinner has plummeted, with contestants’ combined holdings dropping from $148m in May 2025 to $8.6m in this month’s gala.

More than half of the digital wallets publicly listed on the contest leaderboard for Sunday’s dinner are tied directly to crypto exchanges that bar US-based users, indicating they ‌are linked to foreign nationals, according to an analysis of blockchain data prepared for Reuters by the nonpartisan, non-profit consumer advocacy group Public Citizen.

blocks.caption: Demonstrators hold up mock cryptocurrency during a rally Against Trump's crypto dealings at the Trump National Golf Club in May 2025 in Virginia.  Photograph: Jemal Countess/Getty Images for Public Citizen

blocks.text: “Neither the President nor his family ⁠has ever engaged — or will ever engage — in conflicts of interest,” White House spokesperson Anna Kelly told Reuters ​earlier this year. “President Trump proudly made ​the United States the crypto capital of the world ​through executive actions.“

The Trump family’s other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also fallen in value to record ​lows. Together, outside investors in their ‌five main crypto and ​crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5bn​, according to a Reuters analysis.

The Trump meme coin has earned the Trump family at least $635m, according to the president’s June financial disclosure statement. In total, the Trumps had earned at least $2.3bn through April from their four main crypto ventures, including the meme coin.
The president’s stake in a fifth crypto-linked venture, Trump Media & Technology Group, is worth about $430m.
Reuters contributed reporting
